FortiADC object editor

Edit any FortiADC object live in a form, manage its child tables such as pool members, and preview the exact REST request before it is applied.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsnetwork.view network.edit network.apply
📍 WhereFortiADC ADOM → FortiADC → Signatures → policy name, or a classic menu page (/adc/m/<item>?classic=1) → object name (URL /adc/obj/<type>?mkey=<name>)

What is it?#

The object editor opens one FortiADC object read live from the selected device. It shows the object's fields as a form, lists the child tables the object owns (for example a pool's members) and keeps a raw JSON editor for anything the form cannot edit. Form-based saves are dry-run first: you see the exact REST call before anything is sent.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 3.1.0: the sidebar's FortiADC group draws the FortiADC's own measured menu, whose pages open each object in FortiADC's own dialog (see FortiADC workspace). This editor opens from FortiADC → Signatures and from the classic menu pages, which an old /adc/m/<item> address reaches with ?classic=1.

What does it do?#

  • Settings card — every scalar field of the object, with widgets inferred from the device's values: enable/disable becomes a toggle, numbers become number boxes, everything else is text. The identity (mkey) is shown in the page title and is not editable.
  • Structured values (read-only — edit via Raw JSON) — fields whose value is a list or an object. They are displayed but cannot be changed in the form.
  • Child-table cards — one card per child table of the object type (for example Pool Members, Group Members, Match Conditions, Rules). Each row can be saved or deleted, and new rows can be added.
  • Raw JSON — the full object as JSON. Saving from here writes immediately.
  • Create mode — a blank form with a Name (mkey) box. For virtual servers and real servers the form starts with the fields the device requires; virtual servers also show a hint about the dependency chain.

Requirements#

  • A FortiADC selected in the ADOM. Without one the editor redirects to the FortiADC dashboard.
  • The object type must exist in the FortiADC endpoint registry. Unknown types return 404. A type added, re-enabled or disabled on the FortiADC API page is picked up by the editor within 60 seconds, without a restart.

Permissions#

Action Permission
Open an object and read its fields, child rows and raw JSON The legacy view gate, which any read permission grants (for example network.view)
Review & save, Review & create, Save row, Create row, Delete (row), Save raw JSON to device Any key that grants configuration writes, for example network.edit or network.apply

Without write permission the save, create and delete buttons are not rendered, the Add … row panel is hidden and the raw JSON box is read-only. Calling the endpoints directly returns HTTP 403.

How to use#

Edit an object#

  1. Open the object from FortiADC → Signatures or from a classic menu page (/adc/m/<item>?classic=1).
  2. Expand the Settings group and change the fields you need.
  3. Click Review & save. Only the fields you changed are sent to SATOM.
  4. Read the preview: method (PUT), path and the full body.
  5. Click Apply to device. The message Applied to device. appears and the page reloads.

If you changed nothing, the editor says No changes to save.

Create an object#

  1. On the classic menu page (or FortiADC → Signatures), open the right tab and click Create New.
  2. Type the Name (mkey). It is the object's unique identity.
  3. Fill in the fields. Required fields for virtual servers, real servers and pool members are listed in the table under Configuration.
  4. Click Review & create, check the POST preview, then click Apply to device.
  5. The message Created. Opening editor… appears and the new object opens in edit mode, where you can add child rows.

💡Tip

Child tables (pool members, group members, rules…) can only be added after the parent object exists. Create the object first, then add its rows.

Add, edit or delete a child row#

  1. Scroll to the child-table card (for example Pool Members).
  2. To edit a row, expand it, change fields and click Save row, then Apply to device.
  3. To add a row, expand ＋ Add <table> row, fill in the fields and click Create row, then Apply to device.
  4. To delete a row, expand it, click Delete, confirm Delete this row?, review the DELETE preview and click Apply to device.

The add-row form shows the fields SATOM knows the table needs first, then any other fields found on the rows that already exist, plus mkey. For pool members it always offers Real Server (real_server_id, required), Port, Weight and Status, so the first member of an empty pool can be added from the form. For other child tables with no rows yet, the form offers only mkey.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: the add-row form of an empty pool now offers the pool-member fields, including the required real server; before, it offered only mkey and the first member had to be added another way.

Use the raw JSON editor#

  1. Expand Raw JSON at the bottom of the page.
  2. Edit the JSON. It must stay a non-empty JSON object.
  3. Click Save raw JSON to device and confirm Save the RAW object to <device>? FortiADC applies this immediately (no dry-run on the raw path).

⚠️Warning

The raw JSON path writes immediately, without a preview. Use it only for values the form cannot edit, such as lists and nested objects.

Configuration#

Fields the form requires or pre-fills on create:

Object type Field Description Required Default
Virtual Server Interface (interface) Network interface of the virtual server No port1
Virtual Server IP Address (VIP) (address) Virtual IP No (but needed in practice) —
Virtual Server Port (port) Listening port No 80
Virtual Server Profile (profile) Application profile No LB_PROF_TCP
Virtual Server LB Method (method) Load-balancing method No LB_METHOD_ROUND_ROBIN
Virtual Server Load-Balance Pool (pool) Name of an existing pool Yes —
Virtual Server Status (status) Enable or disable No enable
Real Server IP Address (address) Back-end server IP Yes —
Real Server Status (status) Enable or disable No enable
Pool member Real Server (real_server_id) Name of an existing real server Yes —
Pool member Port (port) Back-end port No 80
Pool member Weight (weight) Load-balancing weight No 1
Pool member Status (status) Enable or disable No enable

Virtual server and real server create forms and the pool-member add-row form are pre-filled with these fields (see Add, edit or delete a child row).

Other object types show the scalar fields found on up to three existing objects of the same type. On a device with no objects of that type, the create form only has the Name (mkey) box.

Example#

🧪Example — Add a back-end to an existing pool

  1. Open the classic Real Server Pool page (/adc/m/real-server-pool?classic=1), tab Real Server, and click Create New.
  2. Name rs-web-03, IP Address 192.0.2.33. Review & create → Apply to device.
  3. Switch to the Real Server Pool tab and open pool-web.
  4. In Pool Members, expand ＋ Add Pool Members row, set real_server_id to rs-web-03, port to 8080, then Create row.
  5. The preview shows POST /api/load_balance_pool_child_pool_member?pkey=pool-web. Click Apply to device.

Result#

  • A form save reads the object fresh from the device, merges your changed fields onto it and sends the complete object, so fields you did not see are not dropped.
  • Each applied write is audited (adc.update, adc.create, adc.row_create, adc.row_update, adc.row_delete, adc.delete) with the field names that changed and the appliance.
  • FortiADC applies the change immediately; there is no separate commit step.

Troubleshooting#

"Missing required field(s): pool"#

Possible causes — you tried to create a virtual server without a pool (or a real server without an address, or a pool member without a real server).

Solution — create the pool (and its real servers) first, then enter the pool name. Or use the virtual server wizard, which builds the chain in order.

Verification — Review & create shows the POST preview instead of the error.

"Missing required field(s): real_server_id" when adding a pool member#

Possible causes — the Real Server field of the add-row form was left empty.

Solution — type the name of an existing real server in Real Server (create the real server first if needed), then click Create row again.

Verification — the Pool Members card lists the new row.

"device errcode -56"#

Possible causes — the device refused the write because a value it requires was empty. FortiADC does not name the field.

Solution — compare with an existing object of the same type and fill the missing field; for virtual servers check the pool.

Verification — Apply to device answers Applied to device.

"no changes to save"#

Possible causes — no field differs from the value loaded from the device.

Solution — change at least one field, or reload the page if the device changed meanwhile.

Verification — the preview appears.

"device read failed: …"#

Possible causes — the device could not be read just before the save (SATOM always re-reads the object before building the request).

Solution — check the device's reachability and credentials, then retry.

Verification — the preview appears after the retry.

"row "<id>" not found"#

Possible causes — the child row was deleted or renumbered on the device after the page loaded.

Solution — reload the page and edit the row again.

Verification — Save row shows the preview.

"invalid JSON: …" or "payload must be a non-empty JSON object"#

Possible causes — the raw JSON text is not valid JSON, or is empty.

Solution — fix the JSON syntax; the editor also checks it in the browser first (Invalid JSON: …).

Verification — the status next to the button reads Saved.

Advanced#

Advanced How child tables are found

FortiADC exposes a child table as its own endpoint named <parent>_child_<table>, addressed with ?pkey=<parent name>. SATOM treats every registry endpoint with that shape as a child table of <parent> — as long as <parent> is itself a registered endpoint. No separate list is kept.

Advanced What the form never writes

Keys starting with _ (device-internal flags such as _nondeletable) are never shown or written. List and object values are not sent by form saves; FortiADC keeps absent keys as they are, so those values stay untouched.
